title: Introducing the Dyson WashG1™ wet floor cleaner

hook.text: Dyson's new invention solves the problem of washing hard floors, doing it properly.

summary.tone: Calm, confident, engineering-led premium product launch: clean CG product cinematography, understated VO, minimal text and a restrained black end screen.

signature_moments.description: One continuous 11 s CG camera move that pushes from a wide kitchen shot down to floor level, fades the head shell to a glowing x-ray view and orbits to a macro of the spinning microfibre roller, timed to the 'two microfiber rollers' line.
signature_moments.why_premium: A single unbroken camera path that moves from context to internal mechanism shows technical mastery and explains the product without any on-screen text.

signature_moments.description: The camera dives through the translucent x-ray head into a macro fluid simulation of water and debris on the roller as the VO says 'hygienically cleaning the rollers'.
signature_moments.why_premium: Showing an invisible internal process as a physically plausible simulation makes an abstract benefit (self-cleaning hygiene) concrete and credible.

signature_moments.description: Kitchen, bathroom and living room are chained in one floor-level move using the product and a glass panel passing the lens as wipes, each room landing on its VO noun.
signature_moments.why_premium: Hidden wipes keep the flow continuous and the word-locked room changes make the edit feel scored and intentional.

hook.evidence: Opens straight on the product in use with a clear bold claim naming the problem in the first 5 s (w0-w12); strong but not a surprising or visual-first twist.

clarity.evidence: One idea per beat: claim, two-roller mechanism shown in x-ray, stain removal, self-cleaning rollers, rooms, dock self-clean, tagline. Each visual matches its VO phrase.

ui_showcase.evidence: Not applicable: a physical product launch with no software UI; the product itself is showcased in high-end CG (x-ray cutaways, macro roller).

motion_polish.evidence: Smooth continuous CG camera paths, x-ray material transitions, fluid simulation, hidden wipes between rooms and a block-wipe into a line-draw end screen; no visible jank in the sheets.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchors plus visuals: a steady music bed at 89.1 BPM, integrated loudness -19.04 LUFS, 36 SFX candidates mostly classified music with chimes clustered around the room sequence and end card (x027-x030, x034-x035) and one swoosh_reverse at 6.88 s near the roller macro. Competent and tidy; little evidence of distinct designed SFX for the mechanical moments. Cannot hear the mix itself.

vo_script_quality.evidence: 54 words, concise and benefit-led, with a bookended 'properly' (w12 and w53) tying hook to tagline; the 'sparkly clean' phrase (w42-w43) is slightly casual against the engineering tone.

brand_consistency.evidence: Consistent CG lighting and product materials throughout, Dyson wordmark and geometric sans on the end card and end screen, and engineering-drawing lines in s007 echoing the brand's technical identity.

works_muted.evidence: The visuals show cleaning, rooms and the dock clearly, and the tagline is on screen in s006, but the mechanism details (two rollers, one washes one finishes, self-cleaning) are only spoken; no captions are baked in.

overall.evidence: A tight 26 s product story with best-in-class CG cinematography and clear VO-to-visual mapping, held back slightly by an ordinary sound bed, mechanism info that depends on VO, and a long 10 s static subscribe screen.

localization_friendliness.notes: Only the end card (product name, one-line tagline, wordmark) and the 'Subscribe' end screen carry text, so few frames need re-rendering; the VO is short and over picture without lip sync, easy to re-record, but the mechanism explanation depends on it.

annotation.focal_element: The washG1 cleaner head moving across a bright kitchen floor, later its blue microfibre roller in extreme close-up
annotation.what_happens: One continuous (likely CG) camera move: a wide low-angle tracking shot of a person pushing the cleaner over debris on a white kitchen floor (VO w0-w12 states the problem/promise) pushes in to floor level until the head fills the frame, with a glowing translucent x-ray view of the front rollers; the camera then sweeps around and under to an extreme close-up of the blue microfibre roller spinning (w13-w18 'Two microfiber rollers use clean water'), and pulls back to a three-quarter cutaway showing both rollers and red internals as w19-w23 explain 'one washes, the other finishes'.
annotation.build_rebuild: Render an 11 s single-take product camera path in 3D (low-angle dolly with person, push-in to floor level, orbit to a macro of the spinning roller, pull back to a cutaway) and fade a translucent emissive x-ray material onto the head shell during the push-in.

annotation.focal_element: Cleaner head driving through scattered dirt, then an x-ray cutaway of its rollers and internal tray
annotation.what_happens: Hard cut to a floor-level head-on view of the cleaner advancing over trails of dirt and spills toward camera (w24-w31 'removing tough stains, spills and dried on dirt'); as it nears, the head turns translucent with glowing blue/red x-ray rings, the camera pushes into the cutaway, then dives inside to a macro of water, debris and the blue roller against a red internal surface (w32-w35 'hygienically cleaning the rollers').
annotation.build_rebuild: Animate a CG head driving toward a floor-level camera over a debris decal, crossfade its shell to an emissive x-ray material, then push the camera through the shell into a macro fluid/particle simulation of water and debris on the roller.

annotation.focal_element: A spill of food mess on a white kitchen floor beside a cabinet, cleaner at left
annotation.what_happens: A 0.12 s (3-frame) segment, seen only as one keyframe: the cleaner approaches a spill of food mess beside a kitchen cabinet. It shows the same scene that opens s004, so it may be a detector split or flash frame rather than a separate shot.
annotation.build_rebuild: Cut to the opening frame of the kitchen-spill scene (cleaner at left, debris at lower centre) for 3 frames before the s004 move continues.

annotation.focal_element: The cleaner wiping up mess across successive rooms (kitchen, bathroom, living room)
annotation.transition_other: detector-flagged soft change; appears continuous with the s003 kitchen-spill frame
annotation.what_happens: A floor-level camera follows the cleaner as it clears a food spill along a kitchen cabinet (w36-w37 'leaving kitchens'), carries on into a dark-floored bathroom with puddles (w38 'bathrooms'), then a foreground glass panel/close pass of the cleaner wipes the frame into a wide sunlit living room where a person walks away from the docked cleaner (w39-w43 'and living spaces sparkly clean'); it ends on a low close-up of the head parked on its dock.
annotation.build_rebuild: Chain three room environments in one continuous floor-level camera move, using the cleaner body and a glass panel passing close to the lens as wipe elements between rooms, timed so each room appears on its VO noun.

annotation.focal_element: Docked cleaner head with glowing x-ray rollers and the clear dirty-water tank above
annotation.what_happens: Static-feeling low close-up with a slow push of the cleaner standing in its dock against a wall with soft window shadows; the head shows the translucent x-ray rollers glowing blue and red while the tank shows collected debris, as the VO says w44-w47 'Then it cleans itself'.
annotation.build_rebuild: Hold a 2 s low-angle close-up of the docked product with a slight camera push and pulse the emissive x-ray roller rings, with soft window-light shadow gobos on the back wall.

annotation.shot_type_other: product packshot end card with tagline and wordmark
annotation.focal_element: Left-aligned product name and tagline with the upright cleaner standing at right
on_screen_text: Engineered to wash hard floors. Properly.
annotation.typography: Left-aligned stack: product name in a lowercase-led geometric sans, medium weight, set as a coloured accent; two-line tagline in sentence case, light/regular geometric sans, normal tracking, larger than the wordmark; brand wordmark in lowercase bold geometric sans below with generous space. Font guess (low confidence): a custom Dyson geometric sans similar to Futura.
annotation.what_happens: Hard cut to a clean end card: the upright cleaner stands in a soft-lit room at right while the left side holds 'washG1', the tagline 'Engineered to wash hard floors. Properly.' (read exactly by the VO w48-w53) and the dyson wordmark; the frame is static. At about 26.0 s black rectangles begin covering parts of the frame, the start of the transition into s007.
annotation.build_rebuild: Build a static 16:9 end card with the product photo anchored at the right third and a left-aligned text stack (accent product name, two-line sans tagline, wordmark) placed at about 15% from the left edge, exiting with black rectangular block wipes.

annotation.focal_element: Centred-left dyson wordmark with a 'Subscribe' label below, beside a right-hand panel of thin grey engineering dimension lines framing two empty slots
annotation.transition_other: black rectangular block wipe carried over from s006 (blocks of the previous end card still visible at 26.5 s)
annotation.typography: Brand wordmark in lowercase bold rounded geometric sans, white on black, tight tracking; 'Subscribe' in sentence case, light/regular geometric sans, smaller, normal tracking, centred under the wordmark. Font guess (low confidence): Dyson custom geometric sans similar to Futura.
annotation.what_happens: The last black blocks of the s006 wipe clear by about 27.0 s, leaving a black end screen with the dyson wordmark and 'Subscribe' at left (the VO finishes 'floors properly' w52-w53). At right, thin grey technical-drawing lines with arrowheads draw on between 26.5 s and about 28.0 s to frame two stacked empty rectangles (likely platform end-screen video slots); the frame then holds static to 36.0 s with no further motion visible at 2 fps.
annotation.build_rebuild: On a black 16:9 frame, place the white wordmark and a 'Subscribe' label at the left third, then draw on hairline grey dimension lines with arrowheads (stroke-dashoffset over about 1.5 s) to outline two stacked placeholder rectangles at the right, and hold for 8 s.

pattern.description: Low-angle, slow-motion macro of the floor cleaner's roller in action: water sprays off the spinning blue roller and cereal debris is flung toward the lens across a glossy red floor, while the narration says 'cleaning'.
pattern.why_premium: High-speed macro photography with shallow depth of field, rim-lit water droplets and a bold red/blue palette makes a mundane cleaning action feel cinematic and visceral, proving the product mechanism visually.

build_hint.gsap: Live footage, no tween rebuild. For a motion-graphics recreation: particle emitter for droplets (gsap.to(particles, {x: 'random(200,600)', y: 'random(-200,100)', opacity: 0, duration: 0.6, ease: 'power2.out', stagger: 0.01})) plus a debris sprite gsap.fromTo({x: 0, scale: 0.6}, {x: 300, scale: 1.4, duration: 0.3, ease: 'none'}); keep playback slow-motion.
build_hint.remotion: Use <OffthreadVideo> with playbackRate < 1 for the slow-mo plate; if recreated, drive droplet positions with interpolate(frame, [0, 18], [...]) linearly and the debris scale with interpolate(frame, [0, 9], [0.6, 1.4]).

events.notes: Live-action product macro footage, not UI; elements are physical (water, debris) and hard to map to taxonomy roles, hence role 'other'. Small diff boxes b02-b06 are water/blur noise and were not listed. Camera verdict none.
